QUOTE: Doxygen then applies the forced `FILE_PATTERNS` list (C/C++, Java, Python, Markdown, Fortran, and so on). The tree-sitter layers route by extension. A file that matches no pattern is walked and hashed but produces no rows.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the resolved scope isn't the whole answer. Within it, a file produces rows only if doxygen's patterns or the tree-sitter front end (routed by extension) can read it, which names the parse-built front end as one of the two filters.
